messages:
maria (ml-lead): starting a thread about the v2.4-quant4 canary. ran 24h AB with 5% traffic. overall metrics look OK, but a tiny cohort 'finance-templates' shows hallucination jump. proposing a slice-specific fallback instead of full rollback. pinging infra + pme for quick call
ajay (infra): how big is that slice? we only act on slices with >= 1k requests in the last 24h per the rollout playbook
maria (ml-lead): slice size = 720 requests, so below hard sample threshold. but precision error increase is big: hallucination_rate went from 0.12% -> 0.95% (delta +0.83pp). p-value borderline, but actionable for customers. wondering about tiebreaker logic for small-but-high-delta slices
taylor (pme): product wants stricter behavior for regulated templates. they asked for immediate mitigation even for small slices if absolute hallucination > 0.5% and delta > 0.5pp. that's what triggered the alert in the dashboard :rotating_light:
rollout-bot: AUTO-ALERT: cohort=finance-templates; new_halluc=0.95%; baseline=0.12%; delta=0.83pp; samples=720; rule=prod-guard-0.5pp; severity=high
maria (ml-lead): current options i see:
- A: targeted route-level fallback: route traffic for requests with header X-SLICE=finance-templates back to v2.3 (non-quant)
- B: increase shadowing / run focused evals on that slice (slow)
- C: silent degrade (reduce traffic weight) for impacted slice only
ajay (infra): implementing A is fastest. we can add a traffic rule in ~10m: ``/routing/set?route=finance-templates&target=stable-v2.3``
taylor (pme): product prefers A for now to reduce customer impact. we need a short incident note and to notify a handful of customers. maria can you post a one-liner for CS?
maria (ml-lead): posting to #customer-success: "We observed elevated hallucination for finance templates on latest quantized model; routing that slice to stable model while we investigate. No user data leak."
ajay (infra): I'll queue the route change and attach canary reason. also recommending we update the automatic fallback rule: add a sparse-slice tiebreaker so slices between 500-1000 samples use absolute threshold=0.5% and delta threshold=0.5pp to decide immediate fallback. current logic uses a strict sample floor which misses these cases
maria (ml-lead): Agreed. new rule proposal:
```
if samples >= 1000: use standard statistical test (p<0.01) + delta>0.3pp
elif 500 <= samples < 1000: if abs_rate > 0.5% and delta > 0.5pp -> trigger targeted fallback
else: noop (collect more data)
```
rollout-bot: PATCH-RECORD: attempted route change for finance-templates -> stable-v2.3 by ajay at 1810000200; status=success
taylor (pme): can we also add an audit log entry in the rollout console that records the thresholds used when the bot triggered? needed for postmortem
ajay (infra): yes. I'll add a checkpoint metadata with rule_id=sparse_tiebreaker_v1, samples=720, delta_pp=0.83, abs_rate=0.95%
maria (ml-lead): follow-ups: 1) run targeted smoke eval on a held-out set for finance templates (200 synthetic prompts) 2) postmortem note with decision rationale 3) propose updated rule in gatebook PR by EOD
taylor (pme): +1 on PR. Also let's notify the enterprise customers on the watchlist; i'll draft email
maria (ml-lead): quick logs snippet from the monitoring pipeline (redacted):
```
[2026-03-22T18:05:02Z] cohort=finance-templates total=720 hallucinations=7 rate=0.00972 baseline_rate=0.0012
[2026-03-22T18:05:03Z] delta=0.00852 pval=0.024 (bootstrap)
```
ajay (infra): thanks. rolling patch applied. will follow up in 30m with telemetry after routing takes effect
maria (ml-lead): thanks team. capturing action items and closing thread once post-PR lands. :thumbsup:
